title: Finite maximum history with its labeled lower-cut realization
statement: Let $V$ be a totally ordered set with least element $\bot$, let $\nu$ be a resolution invariant calculus [def-trf-resolution-invariant-calculus-data], and let $A$ be an embedded rational pair [def-trf-labeled-embedded-resolution]. A finite maximum labeled history consists of a raw history $H$ of finite length $n$, its raw prefixes $H_i$ of length $i$ and maximum extensions $H_i\to H_{i+1}$ [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history]. All prefixes are admissible, their full ambient and intrinsic diagrams, inclusions and ordered centers are identified with the corresponding initial segments of $H$, compatibly with extension and the initial pair. The final strict transform is regular, and $H_i$ is regular exactly for $i=n$. Each extension is labeled by its positive maximum in $L=(V\setminus\{\bot\})^{\mathrm{op}}$, and these labels strictly increase. The data include the labeled resolution tower of [def-trf-labeled-embedded-resolution] realizing $H$: its active labels are precisely these labels; a lower cut $D$ selects the raw stage after the number of active labels in $D$, the empty cut selects stage zero, and cuts immediately before and after label $j$ select stages $j$ and $j+1$. Natural isomorphisms identify both cut diagrams with these raw-stage diagrams, preserving inclusions, initial identifications and the ambient center ideals at active labels. Thus absent labels insert identity stages with unit center, while all earlier ideals remain recorded. The invariant at a cut is the invariant on the selected raw prefix, transported by its specified intrinsic identifications. The prefix-index map is the increasing inclusion of stages $0,\ldots,i$ in $0,\ldots,n$. These are data and conditions only, including $n=0$; no existence is asserted.
